To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the size of query incentive needed to obtain an answer to a rare query in a network is a function of the rarity of that answer and the structure (e.g., degree distribution) of the network; and the criticality of incentive propagation in networks is a function of both the rarity and the structure of queries.

(a) query incentive networks are a new model for information-seeking processes, (b) the size of incentives needed in order to obtain an answer to a rare query is a fundamental question in these networks, (c) this problem exhibits critical behavior when query incentives are propagated along a random tree, (d) this criticality is centered at the branching parameter 2, and (e) the critical behavior is robust to small perturbations of the branching parameter

the critical behavior of incentive propagation in a query incentive network occurs when the probability of branching is 2 and that the critical behavior is characterized by the emergence of a giant component in the network.

the interplay of game theory, network theory, and probability theory, in the context of information-seeking systems.
